title: Naturality of extended external cup components in the left coefficient
statement: Let k be a field [def-weil-field], f:X→Spec k and g:Y→Spec k quasi-compact schemes [def-pc-scheme], G any Y-module, a:F→H any X-module morphism, and cF:T(F)→P(F), cH:T(H)→P(H) cochain maps satisfying IsPicardLeftCechCupComponent [lem-sc-picard-left-cech-cup-component]. Then T(a) followed by cH equals cF followed by P(a). There is no quasi-coherence or affine diagonal hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0BED, equation-kunneth-on-cech and following coefficient diagram; Cohomology Tags 01FD and 07MB. Official pages https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BED and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07MB read.

proof.text: Test each degree after all tensor-total summand inclusions. When either index is outside the natural numbers its extended term, hence its tensor summand, is zero. Otherwise transport the inputs through the extension isomorphisms and test pure tensors and product tuples. The extension-map component formula reduces P(a) to the scalar Cech map. This map acts on each coordinate by the coefficient morphism. The hypotheses identify both cup coordinates.

Use naturality of the first-projection tensor-pullback adjunction unit, then presheaf restriction naturality. They move a through the pulled-back front-face section. Tensor-section naturality moves it through the final tensor, while the back section stays fixed. Thus every coordinate agrees. Tensor, product, coproduct and cochain-map extensionality finish the equality.

lean.statement:
theorem picardLeftCechCupComponent_naturality
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [CompactSpace X] [CompactSpace Y] (G : Y.Modules)
    {F H : X.Modules} (a : F ⟶ H)
    (cF : (picardLeftTensorCechFunctor f g G).obj F ⟶
      (picardLeftProductCechFunctor f g G).obj F)
    (cH : (picardLeftTensorCechFunctor f g G).obj H ⟶
      (picardLeftProductCechFunctor f g G).obj H)
    (hF : IsPicardLeftCechCupComponent f g F G cF)
    (hH : IsPicardLeftCechCupComponent f g H G cH) :
    (picardLeftTensorCechFunctor f g G).map a ≫ cH =
      cF ≫ (picardLeftProductCechFunctor f g G).map a
